page: Amazon Web Services x8g.metal-24xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized instance featuring 96 dedicated ARM64 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory, yielding a 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. The processor layout includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache, backed by hardware AES encryption acceleration. The server includes no local storage and no bundled GPUs, routing all persistence through remote storage while providing a 40 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel computing and throughput capabilities. Multi-core performance reaches top-tier rankings in stress-ng (163,905.02) and Geekbench multi-core (26,349.0), while single-core scores remain in the average tier. Memory throughput is significant, posting 481.49 GB/sec read and 215.99 GB/sec write on large 256 MB blocks, accompanied by top-tier PassMark database operations and 195.55 million Redis SET operations per second. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput also fall into the top decile.

The primary tradeoff of the architecture lies in its reliance on high core count over raw single-threaded execution speed, as seen in moderate single-core Geekbench and compression metrics. LLM inference results show strong generation throughput for medium and large models, but single-threaded prompt processing remains intermediate, and smaller models yield lower generation efficiency. Given the absence of local disks, storage must be managed over the network. The hardware profile is efficient for memory-dense, scale-out ARM-compatible enterprise systems, in-memory databases, large-scale Redis deployments, and compilation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services x8g.metal-24xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized server powered by 96 dedicated ARM64 AWS Neoverse-V2 physical cores at 2.8 GHz and 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory. Offering an expansive 16.0 GB of RAM per core, it features 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, no integrated local storage, and no GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight exceptional multi-threaded compute, memory bandwidth, and caching speed, achieving top-tier scores in multi-core Geekbench, PassMark database operations, and Redis SET throughput. Single-core execution and compression tasks display middle-tier throughput. This bare-metal configuration suits massive in-memory caching tiers, large transactional databases, extensive software compilation workflows, and high-concurrency enterprise workloads tailored for 64-bit ARM architectures.
